description: The bar chart illustrates the difference in average Word Error Rate (WER) from the Whisper large model when various text preprocessing optimizations are applied, comparing the performance of two fine-tuned models: NESAC ft model (orange bars) and SESHA ft model (green bars). The vertical axis lists five optimization categories — “Normalised,” “Add Spacing,” “Remove Spacing,” “Americanisms,” and “Dates” — ordered from top to bottom. The horizontal axis represents the “Difference in Average WER from Whisper large,” scaled linearly from 0.000 to approximately 0.0035, with tick marks at 0.000, 0.001, 0.002, and 0.003. Each optimization has two adjacent horizontal bars, with the orange bar (NESAC) consistently longer than the green bar (SESHA), indicating a larger WER difference for the NESAC model across all optimizations. Specific values are labeled at the end of each bar: for “Normalised,” NESAC is 0.00334 and SESHA is 0.00323; for “Add Spacing,” 0.00319 and 0.00344; for “Remove Spacing,” 0.00311 and 0.00306; for “Americanisms,” 0.00299 and 0.00302; and for “Dates,” 0.00257 and 0.00228. The chart suggests that while both models improve over Whisper large (as all values are positive), the SESHA model generally exhibits a smaller WER difference, implying better performance relative to Whisper large under these optimizations, except in the “Add Spacing” case where SESHA’s difference is slightly higher. The legend at the bottom clarifies the color coding for the two models.
